Hello Everyone,

I would like to start my journey with formalizing mathematics. I have some (limited, actually) experience with how Lean works, dependent types, etc. It would be nice to start practising while writing some code that would be useful.

Which of the following is a real gap in Mathlib and also something not very hard to start with:

  • Gromov hyperbolic spaces (especially 0-hyperbolic spaces and R-trees),
  • semigroup of equidecomposability types (its usage in Banach-Tarski related results),
  • measurable equidecomposability (also in Banach-Tarski, or for more general measurable group actions),
  • some nonarchimedean analysis (spherically complete fields – I noticed that someone is working on it)?

I'd apppreciate all comments and suggestions. Final remark, I'll have to learn naming conventions, the workflow of contributing to projects and technicalities (I have Lean istalled in VSCode).
I haven’t seen much on spaces of non-positive curvature, so you might try experimenting there.

@Scott Carnahan, thanks for the reply. So I might start with Gromov product, delta-hyperbolicity and R-trees.
Sincerely speaking, my interest lies in the delta=0 case and the theory of R-trees.

I've come across this repo https://github.com/Strichcoder/lambda-metric-space/tree/main/src
They define Lambda-trees for a linearly ordered abelian group Lambda. This is a modern approach (e.g., Z-trees are precisely combinatorial trees). However, I havent't seen metric spaces with dist having values in more general structures than R in Mathlib.

As it happens, these generalized metric spaces came up in a recent discussion on spherical completeness. Perhaps it is time a suitable generalization was put into mathlib.

I see that the repo you linked was last touched 4 years ago, and was written in Lean 3. I think there is much more mathlib API for things like intervals in ordered groups now.
